researchStatement: Discovering new materials has driven a paradigm shift in existing science and technology. Our group aims to develop advanced energy materials and understand electrochemical reaction behaviors through rational electrode interface design, structural control, in-situ/operando analysis, and phase-dynamics studies.

researchTopics.description: Electrode surface modification using various inorganic and inorganic/organic hybrid materials. The goal is to tune interfacial stability, transport pathways, and electrochemical reversibility for next-generation energy storage systems.
researchTopics.title: Electrode Surface Modification

researchTopics.description: Electrode structuring with optimal hierarchy and dimensionality. We design electrode architectures that improve ionic and electronic transport while maintaining mechanical and chemical stability during repeated cycling.
researchTopics.title: Electrode Structuring

researchTopics.description: In situ analyses of electrode morphological changes, surface electrochemical reactions, and ionic bulk diffusion. These tools help reveal how electrodes evolve during charge and discharge.
researchTopics.title: In-situ / Operando Analysis

researchTopics.description: Phase dynamics by multi-phase conversion reactions between solid, liquid, and gas. We study reaction pathways and structure-property relationships in conversion-type energy materials.
researchTopics.title: Phase Dynamics
